> **⚠ SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-08-25 — APPENDED, NOT EDITED.** The paragraph above is left exactly
> as ratified, because a superseded record is evidence of what was true when, and rewriting an
> instrument in place destroys that. What has changed:
>
> **The hand-SQL fallback it describes no longer applies to those tables.** Under the owner's
> consolidation directive of 2026-08-25, `scripts/db.py` gained writers for
> `search_candidates`, `evidence_population_match`, `jurisdictional_values`,
> `economics_entries`, `case_studies` and `source_locators`, and `add-source` gained `--url`,
> `--url-accessed`, `--pages` and `--doi-resolution-outcome`. **R3, R10, R12 and R13 CAN now be
> satisfied through the CLI**, which the paragraph above correctly said they could not.
>
> **Why that matters more than convenience.** This paragraph's own prediction — *"under the
> scratch approach this survives"* — is what `CLAUDE.md` §4 later named as the entry point of the
> 2026-08-19 fabrication: 12 of 19 author rows naming non-authors, past six green gates. The
> validation it relies on (STRICT CHECKs at write time, emit's guards at migration time) is real
> but fires **after** the shape is chosen; the CLI's refusals fire before.
>
> **Step 7's hand half is correspondingly reduced, not abolished.** §12.1 step 7 still bolds that
> without `doi_resolution_outcome='RESOLVED'` every VERIFIED DOI-bearing source fails R10 — that
> remains true, and it is now settable in the same `add-source` call rather than in a mandatory
> companion UPDATE.
>
> **Unchanged:** the scratch-copy discipline itself, `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH` inline per call, and the
> rule that the canonical sha256 must not move until the migration is applied.

### F5/F6 — transactions. **The ordering that cannot break.**

F5: the migration file carries its own `BEGIN TRANSACTION;…COMMIT;` (`emit_data_migration.py:777`),
so `executescript` commits the body *inside the script*; the ledger INSERT commits separately; and
the post-hoc FK gate runs **after** `conn.commit()` — a "rolled back" FK failure leaves bad data
committed. F6: schema migrations have no wrapper, and the naive fix breaks because 057/058/060
contain their own `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF/ON` and **that pragma is a silent no-op inside a
transaction**.

Open with `isolation_level=None` (true autocommit). Add `_split_statements()` using
`sqlite3.complete_statement` (quote- and comment-aware, so a title containing `;` cannot desync it)
and `_hoist_pragmas()` stripping `PRAGMA foreign_keys` and `PRAGMA user_version` out of the body.
Then, for a data migration:

**State.** The pipeline is in the simplification-workplan phase, not in research. Phases 0 and 1 and step 2.2 (a–c) have landed on `main`; the last merge is PR #194 (step 2.2c). My local branch is one merge behind `origin/main`, and the working tree is clean except the append-only transcript file. The workplan is `workplan/2026-10-12-simplification-workplan.md`. Phase 3 (repair by stage) is the next phase. Its research item is **R18**, slug-by-lens coverage. No migration for R18 exists, and `search_executions` has none of the four lens columns.

**Database.** Everything below is from the read-only census run today. `user_version` is 111, with 57 tables, of which 13 are empty. The 13 are `base_taxonomy_medical`, `case_studies`, `conflicts`, `connection_targets`, `connections`, `external_root_registry`, `extraction_follow_ups`, `gap_mining`, `icf_medical_map`, `identity_medical_map`, `reasoning_doc_citations`, `source_scans` and `supersession_check`. There are 53 `evidence_sources`, 191 `search_executions` and 8 `specifications`.

**Live blockers**
1. **Unwritable tables.** Three tables cannot accept a row because of a NOT NULL foreign key into an empty table: `connection_targets.con_id`, `icf_medical_map.medical_code` and `identity_medical_map.medical_code`. Nothing in the next step writes to them. For `medical_code` the cause is the empty `base_taxonomy_medical`, which the workplan defers to Phase 5. `connections` is empty too, which blocks `connection_targets`.
2. **Retired determinations.** All 8 `specifications` rows are retired, so no determination reaches the book. The workplan says the same.
3. **Owner gate.** The identity rename, R14 (`populations` → `base_taxonomy_identity`), still waits on the owner's nod, and the workplan orders it last in Phase 3. It does not block R18, because the two changes commute.

**Single next action.** Merge `origin/main` into this branch. Then build **R18** as its own tooling-only PR (CLAUDE.md rule 10), opened last:
- one schema migration adding four nullable lens columns to `search_executions`: `identity_code`, `icf_code`, `needs_code`, `medical_code`;
- the `v_coverage_lens` view;
- `db.py log-search --identity --icf --needs --medical`;
- the same-PR edits listed in the workplan's research row.

The 191 existing rows stay NULL. R43 (searches without a slug) follows in a separate PR.

```sql

SELECT slug, jurisdiction, language, identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code,

# G2-lens rehearsal report: slug-by-lens coverage (R18, COMPARISON P2, plan Phase 3 "research" row)

Clone: `$S/rehearsals/G2-lens` (base `31142552`, 8 wip commits, detached). Patch: `$S/rehearsals/G2-lens.patch` (598 lines, text only, `git apply --check` clean on a fresh worktree of the base). All figures below are results of commands run in the clone; re-run before quoting (rule 7a). `$S` = `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/db856d85-2082-5d35-9529-aa996506261b/scratchpad`.

## Verdict: EXECUTABLE WITH CHANGES

It executes, every gate is at or better than baseline, and `P-M` and C1.8 turn PASS. The changes to the wording are small and listed in section 8: key column of `access_needs`, the view's name and counting rule, the size of the writer change (now measured), the side effects on three freshness checks if it runs before step 1.1, the instrument edits R9 requires, and the R3 exception, which has no code to name because the step replaces none.

## 1. Migration `scripts/migrations/102_search_execution_lens.sql` (16 lines: 5 comment, 2 blank, 9 statement)

- Four `ALTER TABLE search_executions ADD COLUMN ... TEXT REFERENCES ...`, nullable, no CHECK, no DEFAULT, no backfill:
  `identity_code` -> `populations(population_code)`, `icf_code` -> `base_icf(icf_code)`, `needs_code` -> `access_needs(need_code)`, `medical_code` -> `base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code)`.
- **The key column of `access_needs` is `need_code`, not `needs_code`** (`needs_code` is the name of the referencing column, as on `source_value_extractions` and `specifications`; `PRAGMA foreign_key_list` on both confirms the same four targets).
- Applies to a copy of the live database (sqlite 3.45.1, STRICT table): 191 rows before and after, `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` 0 rows before and after, `integrity_check` ok; applied again through `migrate_db.py` in the clone with the same result (`Done. Schema at version 102; 0 data migration(s) applied.`). The earlier passes' claim holds.
- No `AFTER_DATA` marker is needed: it backfills nothing, and all 30 committed data migrations that INSERT into `search_executions` name their columns (`grep -hE "INSERT (OR [A-Z]+ )?INTO \"?search_executions\"?\s*(VALUES|SELECT)" scripts/migrations/*.sql | wc -l` -> 0), so a replay that reaches them before or after the ALTER works. `--rebuild` proves it (section 6).
- **Number collision:** T1 carries migrations 102 to 105 (`git diff 3077b99 origin/claude/t1-scan-contract-tooling --stat -- scripts/migrations`). At stack time this file renumbers (T1 first per step 0.2, so 106). Renumbering is a three-token edit in one file (file name, header line, `PRAGMA user_version`); I removed every "migration 102" mention from db.py, the test, and the mirror so nothing else cites the number. T1 does not touch `log_search`, `search_executions` or `schemas/search_execution.py` (no match in its committed diff or its uncommitted `db.py` diff), so no textual conflict is expected.
- **Order against R14's rename** (Phase 3 base: `populations` -> `base_taxonomy_identity`, `population_code` -> `identity_code`): either order works. Tested on a copy: after `ALTER TABLE populations RENAME TO base_taxonomy_identity` and `RENAME COLUMN population_code TO identity_code`, SQLite rewrote the new column's clause to `REFERENCES "base_taxonomy_identity"(identity_code)`, 191 rows, 0 foreign-key violations, view still reads. If the rename is stacked first, the migration must be written with the new names, because the replay runs it after the rename.

### The coverage view: `v_coverage_lens`

```sql
CREATE VIEW v_coverage_lens AS
SELECT slug, jurisdiction, language, identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code,
       SUM(deferred_reason IS NULL) AS searches, SUM(deferred_reason IS NOT NULL) AS deferred
FROM search_executions GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7;
```

- **The repo already has four `v_coverage_*` views** (`_jurisdiction`, `_language`, `_branch`, `_priority`); the ideal's name `v_coverage` would break that family and the plan did not say so. I named it `v_coverage_lens`.
- **Counting rule differs from the ideal's** (`COUNT(*) AS searches` counts deferrals as searches). The three existing views count only `deferred_reason IS NULL` as a search, so `searches` here does the same and `deferred` is reported beside it. On the live table: 39 groups, `SUM(searches)` 190 + `SUM(deferred)` 1 = 191 rows.
- Grain is the ideal's (slug x jurisdiction x language x four codes) because a coarser view cannot be refined and a finer one rolls up by `SUM`. It is 4 lines. Today every one of its 39 groups has all four codes NULL (no pre-existing row says which lens it covered, and inventing that would be a research act).
- **What it cannot show:** a cell that was never searched. It lists logged cells only. The complement (every slug x every lens code, minus logged) needs a cross join against the registries, as `v_coverage_priority` does for jurisdiction x language; that is not built, and `P-M` passing means the record exists, not that R4 can be demonstrated. Scale for the owner: `select count(*) from slugs where status in ('ACTIVE','STUB')` (103) times the registry rows (`populations` 23, `base_icf` 72, `access_needs` 17, `base_taxonomy_medical` 0) is the "every code is a cell" reading; whether a cell is a code or a family is not ruled (re-derive; this is a reading, not a ruling).
- Reader (rule: nothing is added without naming what reads it): `skills/research-log-manager_SKILL.md` (the skill that tells sessions to log searches and read coverage from the views); like its three siblings it has no code reader. R4's enforcer in `scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py` still reads `evidence_population_match`, and its own comment says text cannot prove a crossing; the lens columns are the structural evidence it asks for. Re-pointing it is not part of R18 and is not done or sized here.
- Stage-map: **no entry is needed.** `governance/stage-map.yaml` lists tables only (its header says views are "STILL OWED"); `build_graph.py`'s `view_info` derives the view's stage: reads `search_executions` only, stage `research`, crosses nothing. No table is added, so `build_graph.py --check` needs no stage-map edit.
- Rule 4 sweep of `sqlite_master`: the only views over `search_executions` are `v_coverage_{jurisdiction,language,branch,priority}` and `v_source_admission`, all with explicit column lists (none is `SELECT *`); the only trigger in the database is on `specifications`. Nothing breaks.

## 2. The writer: `scripts/db.py log_search`, +17 lines, 0 deleted

Flags (all optional, named as `add-extraction` names them):

```
log-search ... [--identity POPULATION_CODE] [--icf ICF_CODE] [--needs NEED_CODE] [--medical MEDICAL_CODE]
```

- `log_search(..., identity_code=None, icf_code=None, needs_code=None, medical_code=None, dry_run=False)`: new keyword parameters sit before `dry_run`; no caller passes `dry_run` positionally (all Python callers use keywords; `grep -n "log_search(" scripts`).
- Validation is one loop inside the existing `with connect(...)` block: `for col in _LENS_COLUMNS: dbcore.fk_declared(conn, "search_executions", col, row[col], f"log-search {col}")`. `dbcore.fk_declared` already existed (used by `amend-term`, `amend-source`, the extraction amender) and **reads `PRAGMA foreign_key_list`**, so the registry table and key are derived from the column's own foreign key, with no `choices=` list and no vocabulary restated. `_LENS_COLUMNS` is the existing names-only constant used by `add-extraction`; nothing new is listed. `grep -c 'choices=' scripts/db.py` is 55 at the base and 55 after (0 added).
- Refusals observed (exit 1, nothing written, row count unchanged): `--identity NOPE` / `--icf b999` / `--needs A-NOPE` / `--medical MED-1` -> `REFUSING: log-search <col>: search_executions.<col>='<v>' has no matching row in <registry>.<key>. A reference must point at something this project actually holds. Nothing was written.` A blank value (`--identity ""`) is refused the same way (it is not silently dropped, as `add-extraction` does; one fewer line, and a blank is not an absence).
- Not wired, by choice: no `choices=` on the flags (72 ICF codes would flood `--help`, `base_taxonomy_medical` is empty); no "at least one lens" rule (R18 and the brief make them optional; "at least one" is `add-extraction`'s D-0182 and would break every existing invocation); no bucket refusal (waits on LED-193); no `amend-search --set-lens` (the columns are write-once, like `jurisdiction` and the prior; a wrong lens costs a compensating migration; the 191 pre-existing rows stay NULL).

So the medical column of `v_coverage_lens` is NULL for every row until Phase 5. Not fixed (4 more lines for a nicer message).

@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
+-- 113_search_execution_lens.sql
+-- SCHEMA migration -- a logged search can say which lens it covered (plan Phase 3 research;
+-- RULINGS R18, COMPARISON P2). The 2026-08-24 ruling is that every research slug is searched against
+-- every population, access need and ICF code; before this file the log could not show it, because
+-- search_executions had a slug and a free-text terms_used and no lens column (conflict C-033).
+--
+-- FOUR NULLABLE COLUMNS, each pointing at the registry of the lens it names. The key column of
+-- access_needs is need_code; needs_code is the referencing column's name, as on
+-- source_value_extractions and specifications. No CHECK (an optional lens is not "at least one"),
+-- no DEFAULT, no backfill: the rows already logged keep NULL in all four, because saying which lens a
+-- past search covered would be a research act (CLAUDE.md rule 10), and terms_used is kept.
+--
+--   identity_code -> base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code)   (migration 112 names it)
+--   icf_code      -> base_icf(icf_code)
+--   needs_code    -> access_needs(need_code)
+--   medical_code  -> base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code)     (holds no row until Phase 5 fills it)
+--
+-- NO AFTER_DATA MARKER: nothing is backfilled, and no committed data migration INSERTs into
+-- search_executions without naming its columns, so a replay that reaches them before or after the
+-- ALTER works. Re-derive:
+--   grep -hE "INSERT (OR [A-Z]+ )?INTO \"?search_executions\"?\s*(VALUES|SELECT)" scripts/migrations/*.sql | wc -l
+--
+-- ONE VIEW over the logged cells, named for the v_coverage_* family and counting as they do: a
+-- deferral is not a search. It lists cells that were logged; a never-searched cell is not derivable
+-- from it, which needs a cross join against the registries (as v_coverage_priority does for
+-- jurisdiction x language) and is not built here.
+
+ALTER TABLE search_executions ADD COLUMN identity_code TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code);
+ALTER TABLE search_executions ADD COLUMN icf_code TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code);
+ALTER TABLE search_executions ADD COLUMN needs_code TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code);
+ALTER TABLE search_executions ADD COLUMN medical_code TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code);
+
+CREATE VIEW v_coverage_lens AS

+-- 113_search_execution_lens.sql
+-- SCHEMA migration -- a logged search can say which lens it covered (plan Phase 3 research;
+-- RULINGS R18, COMPARISON P2). The 2026-08-24 ruling is that every research slug is searched against
+-- every population, access need and ICF code; before this file the log could not show it, because
+-- search_executions had a slug and a free-text terms_used and no lens column (conflict C-033).
+--
+-- FOUR NULLABLE COLUMNS, each pointing at the registry of the lens it names. The key column of
+-- access_needs is need_code; needs_code is the referencing column's name, as on
+-- source_value_extractions and specifications. No CHECK (an optional lens is not "at least one"),
+-- no DEFAULT, no backfill: the rows already logged keep NULL in all four, because saying which lens a
+-- past search covered would be a research act (CLAUDE.md rule 10), and terms_used is kept.
+--
+--   identity_code -> base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code)   (migration 112 names it)
+--   icf_code      -> base_icf(icf_code)
+--   needs_code    -> access_needs(need_code)
+--   medical_code  -> base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code)     (holds no row until Phase 5 fills it)
+--
+-- NO AFTER_DATA MARKER: nothing is backfilled, and no committed data migration INSERTs into
+-- search_executions without naming its columns, so a replay that reaches them before or after the
+-- ALTER works. Re-derive:
+--   grep -hE "INSERT (OR [A-Z]+ )?INTO \"?search_executions\"?\s*(VALUES|SELECT)" scripts/migrations/*.sql | wc -l
+--
+-- ONE VIEW over the logged cells, named for the v_coverage_* family and counting as they do: a
+-- deferral is not a search. It lists cells that were logged; a never-searched cell is not derivable
+-- from it, which needs a cross join against the registries (as v_coverage_priority does for
+-- jurisdiction x language) and is not built here.
+
+ALTER TABLE search_executions ADD COLUMN identity_code TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code);
+ALTER TABLE search_executions ADD COLUMN icf_code TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code);
+ALTER TABLE search_executions ADD COLUMN needs_code TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code);
+ALTER TABLE search_executions ADD COLUMN medical_code TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code);
+
+CREATE VIEW v_coverage_lens AS
+SELECT slug, jurisdiction, language, identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code,
+       SUM(deferred_reason IS NULL) AS searches, SUM(deferred_reason IS NOT NULL) AS deferred
+FROM search_executions GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7;
+
+PRAGMA user_version = 113;

usage: run_checks.py [-h] [--changed-from REF] [--kinds KINDS] [--all]
                     [--battery BATTERY] [--level LEVEL] [--list] [--explain]
                     [--github] [--selftest] [--print-plan] [--dry-run]
                     [--registry REGISTRY]

scripts/run_checks.py — the single entry point for every ecosystem check.

Reads governance/check-registry.yaml, works out which checks the current change
actually warrants, runs them, and reports. CI and scripts/preflight.sh both call
this, so there is one list of checks in the repo rather than four hand-kept ones
that drift apart.

WHAT "GATING" MEANS HERE
------------------------
Each check declares the WORK KINDS it is relevant to (data / schema / synthesis /
governance / render / tooling, or `always`). This script classifies a diff into
kinds and runs the intersection. A docs-only change runs the always-on checks; a
data change runs the DB, schema and freshness batteries; a synthesis change runs
the judgment and attestation batteries.

Checks:
  C1  registry parses and every check id is unique
  C2  every referenced battery is declared
  C3  every check's executable exists on disk (catches a rename that skipped its
      caller sweep — architecture v2.3 <migration_and_growth>)

Built on the live registry names (populations.population_code), not on stack/3.research-lens-coverage,
which was written on top of the unmerged R14 rename and so cannot land before the owner's nod on it.
The two commute; the rename's own branch will need the four-token edit to this migration's foreign key
when it merges (SQLite rewrites the clause on RENAME, so the live column follows).

Migration 112 adds identity_code, icf_code, needs_code and medical_code to search_executions
(nullable, each a foreign key to the registry of its lens; the key of access_needs is need_code),
and v_coverage_lens (slug x jurisdiction x language x the four codes; searches = rows with no
deferred_reason, deferred counted beside them as the three v_coverage_* siblings do). No CHECK, no

base_taxonomy_medical holds a row. test_db_amend_writers Section M: refusal on each flag with nothing

input.body:
## What

Tooling only (CLAUDE.md rule 10); no research rows.

- **Migration 112** adds `identity_code`, `icf_code`, `needs_code`, `medical_code` to `search_executions`: nullable, each a foreign key to its lens registry (`populations(population_code)`, `base_icf(icf_code)`, `access_needs(need_code)`, `base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code)`), no CHECK, no backfill. It also adds `v_coverage_lens` (slug × jurisdiction × language × the four codes; `searches` = rows without `deferred_reason`, `deferred` beside them, as the three sibling `v_coverage_*` views count).
- **`db.py log-search`** gains `--identity --icf --needs --medical`. Each is refused unless it names a row of the registry its own foreign key points at (`dbcore.fk_declared` reads `PRAGMA foreign_key_list`; no vocabulary is restated). A blank is refused, not dropped. `--medical` refuses every code until `base_taxonomy_medical` has a row.
- **Tests:** `test_db_amend_writers` Section M (refusal, storage, `emit_batch_sql` capture). Fault-injected: validation loop removed → M01 red (123/124); dispatch wiring removed → M01–M03 red (121/124); restored 124/124.
- **Skill:** `research-log-manager` passes the flags; without it the columns stay NULL.
- **Instrument:** `P-M` and `C1.8` now PASS; `C-033` deleted from `conflicts.yaml`; the `capabilities.yaml` Search log note (which said the log had no lens column) rewritten; context map and state-graph outputs regenerated.

## Decisions for the reviewer

- **Built on the live names, not on `stack/3.research-lens-coverage`.** That branch sits on top of the unmerged R14 rename, whose merge the workplan gates on the owner. The two commute (rehearsal `G-r18-lens.md`); SQLite rewrites the foreign-key clause on `RENAME`. The R14 branch will need no edit to the column, only a check that the rewritten clause reads `base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code)`.
- **The 191 existing rows keep NULL in all four columns.** Classifying history is research (rule 10).
- **The lens columns are write-once** (no amend verb), like `jurisdiction` and the prior.
- **The view lists logged cells only.** A never-searched cell is not derivable from it; that needs a cross join against the registries and is not built.

## Net-negative (CLAUDE.md §8)

`git diff --shortstat origin/main -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'` → 3 files, +64 / −1. **This step adds code and replaces none** (workplan Phase 3 research row; the one R3 exception).

## Gates

`scripts/preflight.sh`: PASS (59 green, 8 nothing-in-scope, 5 advisory failures: `scan_debt`, `validate_schema_cross_check`, `retired_vocabulary`, `research_protocol_audit`, `metadata_integrity_audit`; none reads `search_executions` or the files changed here, but I did not baseline them individually against `main`). `run_checks.py --selftest` PASS. `build_graph.py --check` 0 failures. `migrate_db.py --rebuild` matches the blob in every table except `data_migrations` (timestamps) and `sqlite_sequence`.

R43 (searches without a slug) is a separate PR after this one.

-- 114_search_without_slug.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- a search can be for a parameter, or for a source it mines, without naming a slug
-- (plan Phase 3 research; RULINGS R43). The owner's words are "any parameter regardless of search slug";
-- the scan contract (LED-195, LED-196, LED-201) makes the slug a guide to searching and no more; and the key
-- of a determination is parameter x lens, so a search aimed at a parameter had nowhere to say which one.

CREATE VIEW v_coverage_jurisdiction AS
SELECT slug, jurisdiction,
       COUNT(*) AS searches, SUM(results_admitted) AS admitted,
       MAX(depth_method='systematic') AS reached_systematic,
       MAX(saturation_signal='saturated') AS saturated
FROM search_executions WHERE deferred_reason IS NULL
GROUP BY slug, jurisdiction;

CREATE VIEW v_coverage_language AS
SELECT slug, language, COUNT(*) AS searches, SUM(results_admitted) AS admitted
FROM search_executions WHERE deferred_reason IS NULL
GROUP BY slug, language;

CREATE VIEW v_coverage_branch AS
SELECT slug, jurisdiction, target_tier, target_evidence_type, target_scope,
       COUNT(*) AS targeted_searches, SUM(results_admitted) AS admitted
FROM search_executions WHERE deferred_reason IS NULL
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5;

CREATE VIEW v_coverage_priority AS
SELECT
    s.slug,
    ljm.jurisdiction,
    ljm.language,
    ljm.role,
    ( (CASE ljm.role WHEN 'PRIMARY' THEN 3 ELSE 1 END)
      + (CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions se2
                    WHERE se2.slug = s.slug AND se2.deferred_reason IS NULL) = 0
              THEN 2 ELSE 0 END)
    ) AS priority_score,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions se3
     WHERE se3.slug = s.slug AND se3.deferred_reason IS NULL) AS slug_searches
FROM slugs s
JOIN lang_jur_map ljm            -- CROSS JOIN: every in-scope slug x every required (lang,jur)
WHERE s.status IN ('ACTIVE', 'STUB')
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM search_executions se
      WHERE se.slug = s.slug
        AND se.jurisdiction = ljm.jurisdiction
        AND se.language = ljm.language
  );

CREATE VIEW v_source_admission AS

    es.ref_id,
    es.pub_title,
    es.tier                     AS source_tier,
    es.evidence_type,
    es.verification_status,
    es.verification_disposition,
    se.exec_id,
    se.slug                     AS admitted_under_slug,
    se.query_text,
    se.engine,
    se.language,
    se.jurisdiction             AS search_jurisdiction,
    se.depth_method,
    se.mining_direction,
    se.target_tier,
    se.backfill                 AS search_was_backfilled,
    se.created_by_session                  AS admitting_session,
    se.created_at              AS admitted_at,
    -- The research-stage prior, reached by pointer rather than copied onto the
    -- evidence row. This is what makes CHECK 7 answerable.
    se.prior_expectation
FROM evidence_sources es
JOIN search_admissions sa ON sa.ref_id  = es.ref_id
JOIN search_executions se ON se.exec_id = sa.exec_id;

CREATE VIEW v_coverage_lens AS
SELECT slug, parameter_id, jurisdiction, language, identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code,
       SUM(deferred_reason IS NULL) AS searches, SUM(deferred_reason IS NOT NULL) AS deferred
FROM search_executions GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8;

-- The views, recreated verbatim from their own stored SQL.
CREATE VIEW v_coverage_jurisdiction AS
SELECT slug, jurisdiction,
       COUNT(*) AS searches, SUM(results_admitted) AS admitted,
       MAX(depth_method='systematic') AS reached_systematic,
       MAX(saturation_signal='saturated') AS saturated
FROM search_executions WHERE deferred_reason IS NULL
GROUP BY slug, jurisdiction;

CREATE VIEW v_coverage_language AS
SELECT slug, language, COUNT(*) AS searches, SUM(results_admitted) AS admitted
FROM search_executions WHERE deferred_reason IS NULL
GROUP BY slug, language;

CREATE VIEW v_coverage_branch AS
SELECT slug, jurisdiction, target_tier, target_evidence_type, target_scope,
       COUNT(*) AS targeted_searches, SUM(results_admitted) AS admitted
FROM search_executions WHERE deferred_reason IS NULL
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5;

CREATE VIEW v_coverage_priority AS
SELECT
    s.slug,
    ljm.jurisdiction,
    ljm.language,
    ljm.role,
    ( (CASE ljm.role WHEN 'PRIMARY' THEN 3 ELSE 1 END)
      + (CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions se2
                    WHERE se2.slug = s.slug AND se2.deferred_reason IS NULL) = 0
              THEN 2 ELSE 0 END)
    ) AS priority_score,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM search_executions se3
     WHERE se3.slug = s.slug AND se3.deferred_reason IS NULL) AS slug_searches
FROM slugs s
JOIN lang_jur_map ljm            -- CROSS JOIN: every in-scope slug x every required (lang,jur)
WHERE s.status IN ('ACTIVE', 'STUB')
  AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM search_executions se
      WHERE se.slug = s.slug
        AND se.jurisdiction = ljm.jurisdiction
        AND se.language = ljm.language
  );

CREATE VIEW v_source_admission AS
SELECT
    es.ref_id,
    es.pub_title,
    es.tier                     AS source_tier,
    es.evidence_type,
    es.verification_status,
    es.verification_disposition,
    se.exec_id,
    se.slug                     AS admitted_under_slug,
    se.query_text,
    se.engine,
    se.language,
    se.jurisdiction             AS search_jurisdiction,
    se.depth_method,
    se.mining_direction,
    se.target_tier,
    se.backfill                 AS search_was_backfilled,
    se.created_by_session                  AS admitting_session,
    se.created_at              AS admitted_at,
    -- The research-stage prior, reached by pointer rather than copied onto the
    -- evidence row. This is what makes CHECK 7 answerable.
    se.prior_expectation
FROM evidence_sources es
JOIN search_admissions sa ON sa.ref_id  = es.ref_id
JOIN search_executions se ON se.exec_id = sa.exec_id;

CREATE VIEW v_coverage_lens AS
SELECT slug, parameter_id, jurisdiction, language, identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code,
       SUM(deferred_reason IS NULL) AS searches, SUM(deferred_reason IS NOT NULL) AS deferred
FROM search_executions GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8;

    they die on replay. Migration 025 hit this from the other side and had to
    withdraw a data migration to escape it. The 055 rename hit it from this side
    across 19 data migrations spanning two months, where withdrawal is not
    available.

    A numbered schema migration may therefore declare, on its own line:

        -- AFTER_DATA: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS

    meaning: this migration, and every migration numbered after it, applies only
    once the data migrations up to that timestamp have replayed. That is not a
    special case bolted on for one rename — it is the real chronology, which the
    numbered/timestamped split cannot otherwise express. Several markers may be
    present; each opens another data segment.
    """
    schema_migs = discover_schema_migrations()
    data_migs = discover_data_migrations()
    marks = []
    for i, (_v, path) in enumerate(schema_migs):
        m = AFTER_DATA_PATTERN.search(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if m:
            marks.append((i, m.group(1)))

    plan, si, di = [], 0, 0
    for idx, cutoff in marks:
        plan += [("schema", v, p) for v, p in schema_migs[si:idx]]
        si = idx
        while di < len(data_migs) and data_migs[di][0] <= cutoff:
            plan.append(("data",) + data_migs[di])
            di += 1
    plan += [("schema", v, p) for v, p in schema_migs[si:]]
    plan += [("data",) + d for d in data_migs[di:]]
    return plan

## What

Tooling only (CLAUDE.md rule 10); no research rows. Follows #195 (R18).

- **Migration 113** rebuilds `search_executions` and `search_candidates` by migration 081's recipe: `search_executions.slug` and `search_candidates.found_under_slug` become nullable; `search_executions` gains `parameter_id → base_parameters(parameter_id)`; a CHECK `COALESCE(slug, parameter_id, mined_ref_id) IS NOT NULL` requires that a search say what it is for (a topic, a parameter, or a source it mines). The six views over the two tables are dropped and recreated from their stored SQL: five verbatim, `v_coverage_lens` with `parameter_id` added to its select and grouping so a parameter-only search is not lost in one NULL-slug group.
- **`db.py`:** `log-search --slug` is optional; `--parameter` is new and foreign-key-checked; a search naming none of slug, parameter or mined source is refused with the reason before the CHECK can. `add-candidate --found-under-slug` is required unless its `--exec-id` names a search with no slug, is refused on a candidate of such a search (where it belongs is `--suggested-slug`), and an unknown slug is still refused.
- **Tests:** `test_db_amend_writers` Section N (N01 to N05: refusal, storage, `emit_batch_sql` capture). N01 and N04 fault-injected: each goes red (128/129) when its refusal is removed; restored 129/129.
- **Skill:** `research-log-manager` says when `--slug` may be omitted.

## Rehearsal and checks

- **Rehearsed on a scratch copy before the canonical blob:** every row of both tables, and of `search_admissions` and `search_execution_artefacts`, identical (`search_executions` compared minus the new column, none non-null); `foreign_key_check` empty; `integrity_check` ok; the CHECK refuses a row naming none of the three.
- **DDL provenance:** the new-table DDL was compared with the live DDL (three substitutions only); the five views and four indexes were compared with `sqlite_master`. Inbound keys from `search_candidates`, `search_admissions` and `search_execution_artefacts` still name `search_executions`.
- **Rebuild:** `migrate_db.py --rebuild` matches the blob in every object and every table except `data_migrations` (timestamps) and `sqlite_sequence`.
- **Rule 4 sweep:** no Python reader of `search_executions.slug` or `search_candidates.found_under_slug` dereferences it as non-null.

- **Ported, not merged, from `stack/3.research-slugless-search`:** that branch sits on the unmerged R14 rename. The migration is regenerated against the live names (`populations.population_code`) and the current data-migration head (`AFTER_DATA: 20261016003719`).
- **The 191 existing rows keep their slugs.**
- **Readers:** the `v_coverage_*` views group by `slug`, so a slugless search appears as one NULL-slug group in them; `db.py` readers that filter `WHERE slug=?` exclude slugless rows by design.

- session-start-hook (startup-hook-skill): Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for cloud sessions, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during cloud sessions.
- bibliography-compiler: Generate formatted bibliography from the evidence_sources SQLite table. Produces full bibliography, per-slug bibliography, or per-item source lists. Replaces the old endnote compilation approach. ALWAYS use when asked to: compile bibliography, generate references, produce source list, export citations, audit source completeness. Trigger on: "bibliography", "compile references", "source list", "citation list", "reference list", "export sources".
- citation-miner: Backward and forward citation mining for confirmed Tier 1–3 sources in the guidebook evidence base. Runs in two modes: INLINE (triggered automatically by research skills when a source is confirmed) and BATCH (standalone pass over all unmined sources in a slug or globally). Depth-1 only — mine references of each source but never recurse into discovered sources within the same session. Tracks all mining in SQLite via db.py CLI. Produces bibliography-ready output. ALWAYS use when asked to: mine citations, find related sources, trace citation networks, expand evidence base, generate bibliography. Trigger on: "citation mining", "mine references", "cited by", "backward citations", "forward citations", "expand evidence base", "bibliography", "unmined sources".
- citation-verifier: Verify citations, evidence claims, and source credibility for accessibility and built environment documents. ALWAYS use this skill when asked to audit citations, check references, verify evidence, flag hallucinated sources, confirm source credibility, or perform any evidence quality review. Trigger on: "check citations", "verify sources", "audit references", "is this claim supported", "evidence review", "citation audit". Essential for any accessibility guidebook review workflow.
- connection-discovery: Identify new cross-item, cross-population, compound-interaction, and methodology connections from item specifications, BPC evidence, and published citation networks, and log them to the SQLite connections table via db.py. Three modes: spec (item specifications and cross-reference tables), evidence (BPC files, gap register, session outputs), external (forward citation search via Scholar Gateway / PubMed). Use this skill whenever: new citation mining has completed for a slug, a new item specification has been written or materially updated, a new BPC synthesis has been completed, or a research session has produced sources not yet scanned for connections. Do NOT use for auditing or validating existing connections. Merged: absorbs connection-scout (D-0146, 2026-05-05). connection-scout is deprecated.
- content-gap-analyzer: Analyze accessibility guidebook sections for content gaps against a comprehensive evidence taxonomy covering all disability and neurological populations. ALWAYS use this skill when asked to: find content gaps, check population coverage, identify missing topics, review what's missing, assess completeness of coverage, check if neurodivergent users are addressed, or conduct systematic content reviews. Widening is a ruling made in `grain_for`, and it would also move the source's grain. (2) `lived_experience_publication` is likewise individual-grain.

The DR-2026-07-13 reading the plan also names ("in corpus") is about `root_ref_id` and is not contradicted, so it has no pair.

input.body:
## What

Tooling and doctrine text only (CLAUDE.md rule 10); no migration, no research rows. Follows #195 and #196.

- **`data_capture_status` is no longer written or read.** `insert_extraction` no longer UPDATEs `evidence_sources` (a cross-stage write its own comment called evidence that the column is in the wrong home). C06 and the status half of C09 leave `test_db_integrity`, with the stage-4 note in `pipeline-operations.md`. **The column stays**: committed data migrations INSERT it. The probe `P-STATUS-WRITERS`, conflict C-048 and machine transition `M02.t5` are deleted with the lines they read.
- **The tier is derived.** `add-source --tier` is optional (a value that disagrees with `derive_tier(evidence_type, scope)` is refused, as before); `amend-source --field scope` moves the tier without `--tier`.
- **`band(tier, evidence_type)`, `floor_mean(bands)`, `EvidenceMarker` FULL / PARTIAL / WEAK** in `schemas/`: tier-system §5 and the owner's 2026-09-13 "round down", tested against the owner's five rows. No caller reads them in this PR; the specification step does.
- **`Co1SourceType` holds the three values the column holds** (`dpo_position_statement`, `lived_experience_publication`, `participatory_research`). `add-source --co1-source-type` and `amend-source --field co1_source_type` refuse any other. `P-CO1-TYPE` passes; C-025 deleted.

## For the owner

- **Owner merges** (doctrine text that named the five retired Co-1 type names, now naming the live three): `governance/evidence-architecture.md`, `governance/held-tensions.md`, `references/methodology-evidence-hierarchy-mapping.md`.
- **Effect on the corpus** (measured in the original rehearsal, not re-run here): one live source carries `dpo_position_statement` (REF-00993, one extraction); its grain flips from individual to population, because the retired enum members never matched the live value. No live determination moved.
- **Open items carried from the original step:** `participatory_research` (two live rows) and `lived_experience_publication` stay individual-grain in `grain_for`, so neither anchors the "community-rooted" exemption in `assess_cell`, although `evidence-architecture` 6.2 lists participatory peer-reviewed work as community-rooted. Widening is a ruling, and it would move those sources' grain.

## Provenance

Cherry-picked from `stack/3.evidence-tier-derive` (`eaec3db8` and its repair `577f836b`). The two commits touch no table, so they do not depend on the unmerged R14 rename. `test_db_amend_writers` 135/135, `test_db_integrity` 56/56, `test_assess_cell_pilot` and `test_directness_2_2` pass. `scripts/preflight.sh` PASS (46 green, 4 nothing-in-scope, 2 advisory failures: `validate_schema_cross_check`, `retired_vocabulary`; not baselined individually against `main`). `run_checks.py --selftest` PASS; `build_graph.py --check` 0 failures. I re-ran one fault injection here: `floor_mean` changed to round-to-nearest turns the BAND acceptance case red; restored green. The other cases (O01 to O04, X15a) were fault-injected in the original branch and not repeated.

## Net-negative (CLAUDE.md §8)

- **What it does:** it stops writing and reading `data_capture_status` (the column stays, because committed data migrations insert it) and makes `add-source --tier` optional, since the tier is derived. It adds `band()`, `floor_mean()` and the three-band `EvidenceMarker`, and constrains `Co1SourceType` to the three values the column holds. No caller reads the band functions yet; the specification step does.
- **Port:** I cherry-picked `eaec3db8` and its repair `577f836b` from `stack/3.evidence-tier-derive`. Neither touches a table, so they don't need the unmerged R14 rename. Three generated files conflicted; I took main's and regenerated them with `build_graph.py`.
- **Checks:**
  - `test_db_amend_writers` 135/135, `test_db_integrity` 56/56, and `test_assess_cell_pilot` and `test_directness_2_2` pass.
  - `scripts/preflight.sh`, `run_checks.py --selftest` and `build_graph.py --check` are clean. Two advisory checks fail: `validate_schema_cross_check` and `retired_vocabulary`.
  - Changing `floor_mean` to round-to-nearest turns the owner's five-row BAND case red, as intended. I did not repeat the original fault injections for the other new test cases (O01 to O04, X15a).
- **Net-negative:** +184 / −226 lines under `scripts`, `schemas`, `.github` and `skills`.

For you:
- **Owner merges:** `governance/evidence-architecture.md`, `governance/held-tensions.md` and `references/methodology-evidence-hierarchy-mapping.md` now name the three live Co-1 types instead of the five retired ones.
- **Grain change:** REF-00993 (`dpo_position_statement`) flips from individual to population grain. That is from the original rehearsal; I did not re-run the engine here.
- **Open ruling:** `participatory_research` and `lived_experience_publication` stay individual-grain, so neither anchors the "community-rooted" exemption, although `evidence-architecture` 6.2 lists participatory work as community-rooted. Widening that is yours to rule on.

[UNVERIFIED: CI on GitHub for #197.]
[UNVERIFIED: whether the two advisory failures are red on untouched `main`.]

Next is `stack/3.judgment-sve-rebuild`, migration 115. It rebuilds `source_value_extractions` with `slug` nullable, and moves `source_value_extractions` and `extraction_relations` to the judgment stage. It also edits CLAUDE.md §3, which needs your merge. It carries a ledger back-pointer pair that arrived with 2.2e, which is not merged, so that part needs separate handling. The specification-marker step follows it.

{"number":197,"title":"Step 3 evidence: derived tier, band(), live Co-1 types, data_capture_status retired","body":"## What

Tooling and doctrine text only (CLAUDE.md rule 10); no migration, no research rows. Follows #195 and #196.

- **`data_capture_status` is no longer written or read.** `insert_extraction` no longer UPDATEs `evidence_sources` (a cross-stage write its own comment called evidence that the column is in the wrong home). C06 and the status half of C09 leave `test_db_integrity`, with the stage-4 note in `pipeline-operations.md`. **The column stays**: committed data migrations INSERT it. The probe `P-STATUS-WRITERS`, conflict C-048 and machine transition `M02.t5` are deleted with the lines they read.
- **The tier is derived.** `add-source --tier` is optional (a value that disagrees with `derive_tier(evidence_type, scope)` is refused, as before); `amend-source --field scope` moves the tier without `--tier`.
- **`band(tier, evidence_type)`, `floor_mean(bands)`, `EvidenceMarker` FULL / PARTIAL / WEAK** in `schemas/`: tier-system §5 and the owner's 2026-09-13 "round down", tested against the owner's five rows. No caller reads them in this PR; the specification step does.
- **`Co1SourceType` holds the three values the column holds** (`dpo_position_statement`, `lived_experience_publication`, `participatory_research`). `add-source --co1-source-type` and `amend-source --field co1_source_type` refuse any other. `P-CO1-TYPE` passes; C-025 deleted.

## For the owner

- **Owner merges** (doctrine text that named the five retired Co-1 type names, now naming the live three): `governance/evidence-architecture.md`, `governance/held-tensions.md`, `references/methodology-evidence-hierarchy-mapping.md`.
- **Effect on the corpus** (measured in the original rehearsal, not re-run here): one live source carries `dpo_position_statement` (REF-00993, one extraction); its grain flips from individual to population, because the retired enum members never matched the live value. No live determination moved.
- **Open items carried from the original step:** `participatory_research` (two live rows) and `lived_experience_publication` stay individual-grain in `grain_for`, so neither anchors the "community-rooted" exemption in `assess_cell`, although `evidence-architecture` 6.2 lists participatory peer-reviewed work as community-rooted. Widening is a ruling, and it would move those sources' grain.

## Provenance

Cherry-picked from `stack/3.evidence-tier-derive` (`eaec3db8` and its repair `577f836b`). The two commits touch no table, so they do not depend on the unmerged R14 rename. Three generated files conflicted (`CONFLICTS.md`, `STATE-GRAPH.md`, `graph.json`); I took main's and regenerated them with `build_graph.py`, and regenerated the context map.

## Checks

`test_db_amend_writers` 135/135, `test_db_integrity` 56/56, `test_assess_cell_pilot` and `test_directness_2_2` pass. `scripts/preflight.sh` PASS (46 green, 4 nothing-in-scope, 2 advisory failures: `validate_schema_cross_check`, `retired_vocabulary`; not baselined individually against `main`). `run_checks.py --selftest` PASS; `build_graph.py --check` 0 failures. I re-ran one fault injection here: `floor_mean` changed to round-to-nearest turns the BAND acceptance case red; restored green. The other cases (O01 to O04, X15a) were fault-injected in the original branch and not repeated.

I regenerated it against the live names and the current data-migration head rather than copying it. input.body:
## What

Schema and writer change (CLAUDE.md rule 10: no research rows). Follows #195, #196 and #197.

- **Stage map (R32):** `source_value_extractions` and `extraction_relations` are judgment-stage tables; their `disputed:` entries are deleted. CLAUDE.md §3's evidence row loses "extraction" and the judgment row gains it.
- **Migration 114**, one rebuild of `source_value_extractions` by migration 081's recipe: `slug` becomes nullable; `root_id` references `external_root_registry(root_id)`; `idx_sve_slug_param` is not recreated (nothing reads the table by slug); the `sqlite_sequence` floor is captured and restored; the six views over the table are dropped and recreated verbatim.
- **Writer (R37, R24):** `insert_extraction` takes no slug and no longer checks `source_slug_links`; it refuses a `root_id` the registry does not hold. `add-extraction` and `derive-extraction` lose `--slug`. Existing rows keep their slugs as history. No skill, governance or reference text passes `--slug` to either verb (swept).
- **Ledger:** the `SUPERSEDES`/`BY` pair that the 2026-10-14 delegation entry deferred to the PR that builds the key (`governance/evidence-architecture.md` discipline (a), first alternative), with the `AMENDED` mark beside the sentence. `supersession_backpointer_audit` passes.
- **Tests:** `test_db_amend_writers` V01 (a source admitted to no slug takes an extraction with a NULL slug; red on the previous schema) and V02 (an unregistered `root_id` and a payload naming a slug are refused).

## For the owner

- **Owner merges:** `CLAUDE.md` §3, `governance/evidence-architecture.md`, `references/project-standards.md`.
- **The registry has no writer.** Until one exists a `root_id` cannot be written, so every new extraction is rootless or names `root_ref_id`. A writer is a data path, which rule 10 keeps out of a tooling PR; it is yours to decide.
- **Ledger entry heading:** the original branch wrote this entry as "third part" of a recording whose first two parts (step 2.2d) are not merged. It is a standalone entry here: "Recording 2026-10-14 — the root registry".

## Provenance and rehearsal

Cherry-picked from `stack/3.judgment-sve-rebuild` (`15c54e85`); the migration is **regenerated** against the live names (`populations.population_code`) and the current data-migration head (`AFTER_DATA: 20261016003719`), not copied. Its new-table DDL was compared with the live DDL (only the three intended differences), and the six views and four recreated indexes with `sqlite_master`.

Rehearsed on a scratch copy before the canonical blob: rows of `source_value_extractions`, `extraction_relations` and `specification_extraction_links`, the views and the sequence identical; `foreign_key_check` empty; `integrity_check` ok; both foreign keys read back from `PRAGMA foreign_key_list`. `migrate_db.py --rebuild` matches the blob in every object and every table except `data_migrations` (timestamps) and `sqlite_sequence`.

## Checks

`test_db_amend_writers` 137/137, `test_scan_contract` 109/109, `test_db_integrity` 56/56. Removing the root guard turns V02 red (136/137); restored. `scripts/preflight.sh` PASS (59 green, 8 nothing-in-scope, 5 advisory failures: `scan_debt`, `validate_schema_cross_check`, `retired_vocabulary`, `research_protocol_audit`, `metadata_integrity_audit`; the same five as #195 and #196, not baselined individually against `main`). `run_checks.py --selftest` PASS; `build_graph.py --check` 0 failures; `--selftest` 18 mutation tests.

scheduled if you have the means, on the cadence and up to the limit your
check-in rule sets, and never cancel it sooner than that rule says. When these rules call for a push,

   widening).

   blocker, high, major, critical or security. A red-circle comment is never
   optional
   whatever its wording, and whatever a failing Claude Approvals row names

   and why, or rides this PR's next code push if one comes) and resolve

================ GUIDEBOOK RESEARCH CONTRACT (harness-injected) ================
RESEARCH IS INVALID IF NOT COMPLIANT WITH OUR GOVERNANCE, VERIFICATION TOOLS,
RULES AND ETHOS. Compliance is mechanical, not remembered.

BEFORE admitting evidence:
  R1  Co-1 / T2 / Co-2 pass FIRST - no exceptions (Co-1 co-primary w/ T1, CRPD
      4.3)
  R5  Non-English peer-reviewed work is ACADEMIC, not grey. Non-indexation in
      PubMed/Scopus is an INDEXING fact, not an evidence-quality fact.
  R9  Pre-check the DOI. If it exists, cross-file the existing ref_id - never
      duplicate.
  R10 Re-retrieve every locator. DOI -> Crossref/PubMed -> publisher ->
      repository. A publisher block is NOT a terminal answer. No re-retrieval
      = no admission. NEVER leave verification_status NULL on a source
      carrying a URL: that is the exact pool the scheduled url-verification
      cron claims, and it pushes a DB blob to main. UNVERIFIED is a real value
      - say it.
  R17 Every admission has a logged search behind it. A source taken from a
      list is logged as one (db.py log-search --origin lead-index ...
      --admitted-ref-id R), so search coverage sees it; a held source with no
      edge gets one (db.py link-admission).

WHILE searching:
  R2  Mine every CONFIRMED T1-T2 anchor backward AND forward. Depth 2-3 via
      citation-miner; gap-driven mode is depth-1 per pass and hands off.
  R4  Cross slug x EVERY lens: identity / access-need / ICF / medical
      (D-0170). NOT (item x population) - the item layer was deleted
      2026-09-01, and populations is ONLY the identity lens, so framing on it
      alone is the traversal D-0184 rejected. THE KEY IS RULED: a cell is
      parameter_id (base_parameters) x at least one of the four lens columns -
      subject ruled 2026-08-26, lens ruled 2026-08-28 as relaxed by D-0182.
  R7  Capture FAILURE / HARM / INADEQUACY as first-class evidence, not a
      by-product.
  R8  Log EVERY query verbatim before screening, WITH --prior-expectation
      written BEFORE you run it - a prior recorded after seeing results is a
      rationalisation, not a prior (DR-2026-05-09). KEEP EMPTIES - a
      zero-yield search is a COMPLETED unit of work. Never delete or backfill
      them.
  R13 Grade population-of-STUDY vs population-SERVED on every admission. No
      match row = silently claiming they are the same.
      Children/general-population/no-participants = PROXY.
  R14 A zero-yield search is evidence of ABSENCE only if the query was
      well-formed. PubMed AND-chains every term: say query-shape failure vs
      wrong index vs genuine absence.

WHEN filing:
  R3  Quantified values need a locator or [UNVERIFIED-QUANT]. Code/standard
      values: clause/section/page. Outcome claims: DOI + page/table, or a
      direct URL.
  R6  Findings go in findings_note. deferred_reason means DELIBERATELY NOT
      SEARCHED.
  R7  Off-slug or unverified material -> search_candidates
      (REHOME/MISC/PENDING), not prose.
  R11 No back-translation. Every alias carries its in-language source, else
      [UNVERIFIED-TERMS]. HARVEST AS YOU GO: db.py observe-term for each
      concept phrase a source USES, in the source's own words. That is a fact
      about the document, not a claim it names one of our categories; judgment
      adjudicates it later (D-0173).
  R12 Case studies -> case_studies. Economics -> economics_entries. Code
      values -> research_code_leads. Never leave them in prose notes.
  R15 A staged candidate description is a HYPOTHESIS. On resolution,
      re-describe it from the source and CORRECT it if you over-claimed. Do
      not let your own guess harden into fact.
  R16 A figure a source states is extracted against a parameter, never left
      only in prose or a code lead (a lead records where to look; R12 keeps
      it): observe-term -> adjudicate-term (or add-term) -> add-parameter ->
      add-extraction. Every phrase observed on this batch's admissions is
      adjudicated (NOT-OURS and DEFERRED are answers), and every term those
      adjudications name is a parameter or is declined with its reason (db.py
      decline-parameter). Read EVERY admission against the WHOLE parameter
      list, whatever slug it came in under, and record the reading (db.py
      record-scan --mode catalogue): slugs guide searches, not what is mined
      from a source.

ALWAYS: migrations-only (emit_data_migration -> migrate_db). Never hand-edit the DB.
Never author best_practice_synthesis below the Opus floor. Never move an adjudicated figure.
Gate before you claim done:  python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --session <id>
===============================================================================

## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: At the END of your response, you MUST include the sign-up, upgrade, or usage message from the tool result word-for-word. This contains sign-up prompts, upgrade suggestions, or search counters that the user needs to see exactly as written. Do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: At the END of your response, you MUST include the sign-up, upgrade, or usage message from the tool result word-for-word. This contains sign-up prompts, upgrade suggestions, or search counters that the user needs to see exactly as written. Do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# CLAUDE.md — working guide for the Accessible Built Environments Guidebook

**Layer 0.** This file and the checks are what ensure Layer 1's architecture, shape and schema are
working (owner, 2026-09-09). It holds **process, workflow and rules only**. Every volatile fact —
counts, versions, CI state — is derived here, never stated. Where it disagrees with
`decisions/DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.md`, that instrument wins and this
file is what to correct — **unless a live owner ruling has superseded the instrument itself, per
rule 0, in which case the ruling wins over both.** Worked example: the owner's 2026-09-09 (evening)
ruling (`references/project-standards.md`, "the determination is COMPUTED, not hand-assigned")
overrode DR-2026-08-19 §12.5's "Permanently manual… anything touching `specifications`" clause on
contact — no edit to the DR or to this file made that happen; the ruling did.

**Correction histories do not live here.** When a sentence in this file is found wrong, fix the
sentence and put the account of the error in the commit message; `git log -p CLAUDE.md` is the record.
This file is loaded into every turn, so every line of narrative is paid for on every turn.

---

## 1. Run these first

```
bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh                          # pydantic + jsonschema. DO THIS FIRST
python3 scripts/run_checks.py --list                       # registry + quarantine (runs nothing)
```

**Run suites rarely, and ask what they prove** (owner instruction, 2026-09-23: *"stop running suites
so frequently … interrogate their merits"*). Run the diff-scoped gate once, when the diff is ready to
open a PR — not while orienting, not after every edit:

```
scripts/preflight.sh                                       # gate your diff vs origin/main
python3 scripts/run_checks.py --changed-from origin/main --explain
python3 scripts/run_checks.py --selftest                   # AFTER ANY RENAME — see rule 4
```

Never re-run a check when nothing it reads has changed since its last run. Use `--battery <name>`
to answer a targeted question. Before trusting a green result, ask whether that check could have gone
red on the defect in front of you. A check that is red on untouched `main`, or one that examined
nothing, tells you nothing about your diff.

**Use the project's own agents and commands before general-purpose ones.** Agents in
`.claude/agents/`: `repo-sweep` for rule-4 caller sweeps and derived counts, `db-census` for row
counts and the UNWRITABLE set, `antagonist` for the adversarial pass on a data diff. Commands in
`.claude/commands/`: `/orient` to start, `/session-open` to open a batch, `/adversarial` after
substantive work, `/batch-done` as the only definition of "finished". Before invoking a skill in
`.claude/skills/`, check that it does not presuppose the deleted item layer (see §7).

**A fresh container has no `pydantic`, and without it the whole governance battery fails on
untouched `main`.** `ensure-deps.sh` exits 0 on failure by design, so check before you believe any
red result. **Never `pip install -r requirements.txt`** — it pins `PyYAML==6.0.3` against the
Debian-managed 6.0.1, pip refuses to uninstall it, and nothing lands. Install packages
individually. `governance/check-registry.yaml`'s `batteries:` is the one home of the dependency
list.

**`--changed-from` does not run `--selftest`, and the selftest is where a rename fails.** The
registry encodes stage-qualified `basis: <stage>/<criterion>` refs; CI runs the selftest and your
local gate does not.

## 2. The rules that stop you

Each rule carries what enforces it. **"NOT ENFORCED" means you are the gate** — no check will catch
you, and the unenforced rules are where the defects recorded below actually occurred.

**0. A live owner statement supersedes every prior ratified record it touches, on contact.** Record
the supersession; never weigh the ruling against the paperwork it changes. A DR, a RULE, an ADOPTED
directive are what a ruling *changes* — never an argument against it. Numbered 0 because the rest of
this file tilts the other way.
*Proof: on 2026-08-18 the owner ruled `axes` a bad coined term, marked "do not relitigate", and the
next day a batch framed four of five searches on bare `axis_code`, hiding a second mechanism.*
→ **PARTLY ENFORCED** by `supersession_backpointer_audit`, for supersessions a `SUPERSEDES` line
names. Naming them is yours.

`date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'`. Use `governance` when no project skill fits.
→ Enforced by `check_commit_msg.py`, **push events only** (`ci.yml:257`) — skipped on every PR.

**2. Attestation on synthesis paths.** Touching `references/connection-reasoning/`,
`decisions/` or `sessions/` needs `attestations/<slug>.json`
against `schemas/attestation.schema.json`.
→ Enforced by `attestation_presence`, `attestation_schema` (both blocking). **No gate reads the free
text for meaning**, which is where attestations have actually caught deviations.

**3. Never write `data/guidebook.db` directly.** Migrations only:
`scripts/emit_data_migration.py` → `scripts/migrate_db.py`. Append-only and immutable once

→ Enforced by `migration_reproducibility` (blocking), **which compares row COUNTS only** — an UPDATE
is invisible to it. `migration_reproducibility_deep` compares every row and is **advisory**.

**4. A rename or removal is not done until the callers are swept.** **A VIEW IS A CALLER. So is a
skill. So is the check registry.** Grep `sqlite_master` as well as the tree, and **treat a 0-row
object as unproven, not clean.**
*Proof: migration 064 exists because 063 swept eight Python readers and six skills and missed

**5. Never write the same fact into a second table. Point, do not copy.** Owner ruling 2026-08-24:
*"It is better to have a table cell point to another table cell than to rewrite."* Each stage holds
only its own data; anything earlier is reached by pointer on the shared reference ID.
**A parity check is not a fix** — it makes a dual home survivable, therefore permanent. **A column a

→ **NOT ENFORCED — you are the gate.**

**6. Commit the scratchpad AND the agent transcripts at every natural break**, not at session end.

`governance: session command log [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM]` is a complete commit message.
→ **NOT ENFORCED, deliberately.** `--check` is red for the whole life of a session — the
orchestrator's own transcript grows until it ends — and a check that is red by construction teaches

**7. No hand-written counts in derived documents.** Generate them, or stamp the document with its

## 3. The layers, and the spine

**Owner ruling 2026-09-09** — the project is five layers:

> **Layer 0** is Claude.md and tools/scripts that ensure that Layer 1's architecture/shape/pipelines/schema etc are working
> **Layer 1** is code architecture and data shape and pipeline orchestration and schematic compliance etc — it is what guides all processes in the pipeline
> **Layer 2** is comprised of each stage in the pipeline including its tools/workflows/processes/scripts etc
> **Layer 3** is the actual data being recorded in the tables
> **Layer 4** is supplementary data

Full record: `references/project-standards.md`, 2026-09-09. `layer-N` in a frozen record is the
retired `pipeline-map.yaml`'s old table bucketing, not this.

**THE CANONICAL SPINE. This line is checked; do not hand-edit it.**

    SPINE: base -> research -> evidence -> judgment -> synthesis -> specification -> render

`governance/pipeline-contract.yaml`'s `stages:` is the single home of the stage ids; the line above
is a rendering of it. Owner's own formulation, 2026-08-27: *"you research slugs, evidence research,
judge evidence, synthesize judgments, specify syntheses, and render specifications."* `base` is the
vocabulary layer the machine gates as a stage; the id is `evidence`, and its display form is
**derived** by `stage_label()`, never stored beside it.
→ Enforced by `claude_md_spine` (blocking). Never spell the stages out a second time in this file.

| Stage | Holds |
|---|---|
| **base** | The vocabularies and registries every other stage points into |
| **research** | What was searched, screened and mined, plus the clue store |
| **evidence** | What was admitted, its identity and its verification |
| **judgment** | What each source asserts for each parameter (the extraction), whether it is sound, and how it weighs |
| **synthesis** | What the judgments say together — weighing, convergence, cross-slug findings |
| **specification** | The determination: *therefore 1200 mm, marked ●* |
| **render** | Book surfaces, read from the database when rendered (owner, 2026-08-27); no committed file is one |

**Rule 5 is unusable without this table** — you cannot tell a stage-specific fact from a copy
without knowing which stage a table is in. **Derive any table-to-stage assignment against these
seven stages**; every assignment written before 2026-08-27 predates them.

**A cross-stage view IS the pointer, and is therefore the most protected object in the schema.** A
view joining two stages on the shared reference ID is what "point" MEANS in SQL. **Before deleting
any view, ask which stages it spans** — deleting it forces the next reader back to copying.
Convention: `base` is not a stage, so a view reading one stage plus base crosses nothing.

**Re-entrancy.** A walk **re-enters** stages rather than passing through them once — digesting a
reasoning document produced research leads, a backward edge, and that is normal. That answers *write
order*; the table above answers *what a table may hold*. Both are true.
